title: Churches are carved from living rock
summary: At Lalibela in Ethiopia, builders carved churches directly into rock, connecting them with trenches and passages. The ensemble became an important setting for Christian pilgrimage and religious practice.

claims.text: At Lalibela in Ethiopia, builders carved churches directly into rock, connecting them with trenches and passages. The ensemble became an important setting for Christian pilgrimage and religious practice.
The institutional description spans twelfth- and thirteenth-century attributions; no exact foundation year is asserted.

Excavated architecture invites comparison with other rock-cut religious sites. Its historical interpretation also requires distinguishing attributed royal patronage from the individual construction phases of the churches.
